glossary.definition: Bond formed by sharing of electron pairs between atoms.
Property of carbon to form long chains and rings by bonding to other carbon atoms.
Carbon has valency four — forms four covalent bonds.
Compound containing only carbon and hydrogen.
Family of compounds with same functional group, differing by CH₂.
Specific atom/group that determines chemical properties of an organic compound.
Contains only single C–C bonds (e.g. alkanes).
Contains double or triple C–C bonds (e.g. alkenes, alkynes).
Cluster of soap/detergent molecules that traps oily dirt in water.

concepts.name: What is carbon?
concepts.simple_answer: Carbon is a non-metal element (atomic number 6) that forms the backbone of millions of organic compounds in living and non-living matter.
concepts.why: Foundation of Ch 4 — carbon introduced first.
concepts.example: Coal, diamond, graphite, and all living tissues contain carbon.
concepts.remember: C = element 6; organic chemistry is chemistry of carbon compounds.
concepts.common_confusion: Not every compound with carbon is organic — CO₂ and carbonates are exceptions.

concepts.name: Why study carbon compounds?
concepts.simple_answer: Carbon compounds are essential for food, fuel, medicines, plastics, and all life — making this chapter central to science and daily life.
concepts.example: Petrol, proteins, sugar, and cotton are carbon-based.
concepts.remember: Carbon compounds touch every part of daily life.
concepts.common_confusion: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds; inorganic includes others.

concepts.name: Organic vs inorganic compounds
concepts.simple_answer: Organic compounds contain carbon (usually C–H bonds); inorganic compounds include water, salts, and minerals — NCERT focuses on key organic families.

visual.formula: Organic: C–H bonds (generally) | Inorganic: salts, minerals

concepts.example: Methane CH₄ is organic; NaCl is inorganic.
concepts.remember: Organic = carbon compounds; exceptions like CO₂ noted later.
concepts.common_confusion: Urea and CO are borderline cases — NCERT treats most C-compounds as organic.

concepts.name: Unique nature of carbon — preview
concepts.simple_answer: Carbon is tetravalent (4 valence electrons) and shows catenation (self-linking) — together these explain millions of compounds.
concepts.example: Carbon chains in proteins and petrol molecules.
concepts.common_confusion: Silicon also catenates but less than carbon.

concepts.name: Covalent bonding in carbon — preview
concepts.simple_answer: Carbon shares electrons to complete its octet — forms covalent bonds with other carbon atoms and with H, O, N, halogens.
concepts.why: Leads to Day 2 electron dot structures.
concepts.example: In methane CH₄, carbon shares 4 electron pairs.
concepts.remember: Carbon shares electrons — does not form ions easily.
concepts.common_confusion: Ionic bonding is rare for carbon — covalent dominates.

concepts.name: Sources of carbon compounds
concepts.simple_answer: Carbon compounds come from living sources (plants, animals), fossil fuels (coal, petroleum), and laboratory synthesis.
concepts.example: Petroleum distillation gives petrol, diesel, kerosene.
concepts.common_confusion: Fossil fuels are ancient carbon compounds.

concepts.name: Carbon in living organisms
concepts.simple_answer: All living things are built from carbon compounds — carbohydrates, proteins, fats, and nucleic acids all contain carbon chains.
concepts.example: Glucose C₆H₁₂O₆ and amino acids are carbon compounds.
concepts.common_confusion: Carbon cycle links living and non-living carbon.

concepts.name: Fossil fuels and carbon
concepts.simple_answer: Coal and petroleum are complex mixtures of carbon and hydrogen compounds formed over millions of years from ancient life.
concepts.example: Burning petrol releases CO₂ and H₂O.
concepts.common_confusion: Incomplete combustion of fuels produces CO and soot.

concepts.name: NCERT Chapter 4 scope
concepts.simple_answer: Ch 4 covers bonding, allotropes, hydrocarbons, functional groups, reactions, ethanol, ethanoic acid, and soaps.
concepts.example: Activities on burning, bromine water, and soap micelles.

concepts.name: Chapter 4 opening — jesc104
concepts.simple_answer: NCERT Class 10 Science Chapter 4 (jesc104.pdf) introduces carbon's versatility before detailed bonding and reactions.
concepts.example: Refer to NCERT for electron dot diagrams.
concepts.remember: Start with why carbon is special.
concepts.common_confusion: Chapter builds from structure to applications.

days.title: Bonding in Carbon — Covalency and Electron Dot Structures

concepts.name: Covalent bond definition
concepts.simple_answer: A covalent bond forms when two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons to achieve stable electron configuration.
concepts.example: H–H in H₂ molecule shares one electron pair.
concepts.common_confusion: Sharing completes octet (or duplet for H).

concepts.name: Why carbon forms covalent bonds
concepts.simple_answer: Carbon has 4 valence electrons — it shares electrons rather than losing or gaining four, forming strong covalent bonds.
concepts.example: Carbon never forms C⁴⁺ or C⁴⁻ in normal compounds.
concepts.common_confusion: Carbon can form single, double, and triple bonds.

concepts.name: Tetravalency of carbon
concepts.simple_answer: Tetravalency means carbon has a valency of four — it forms four covalent bonds in most compounds.
concepts.example: In CH₄, carbon bonds to four hydrogen atoms.

concepts.name: Electron dot structure of CH₄
concepts.simple_answer: Methane CH₄: carbon shares one electron pair with each of four H atoms — four single covalent bonds.
concepts.example: Main component of natural gas.
concepts.remember: C in centre; 4 H around; 4 shared pairs.
concepts.common_confusion: Each bond is one shared pair (single bond).

concepts.name: Electron dot structure of C₂H₆
concepts.simple_answer: Ethane C₂H₆: two carbon atoms joined by a C–C single bond; each C also bonded to three H atoms.
concepts.example: Ethane is second member of alkane series.
concepts.remember: Two C atoms single-bonded; 6 H total.
concepts.common_confusion: C–C single bond = one shared pair.

concepts.name: Electron dot structure of O₂
concepts.simple_answer: Oxygen O₂: each O atom shares two electron pairs with the other — a double bond (O=O).
concepts.example: O₂ needed for combustion and respiration.
concepts.common_confusion: O₂ has 6 valence electrons per atom.

concepts.name: Electron dot structure of N₂
concepts.simple_answer: Nitrogen N₂: two N atoms share three electron pairs — a triple bond (N≡N), very stable molecule.
concepts.example: N₂ makes up 78% of air.
concepts.common_confusion: N≡N is very strong — explains N₂ inertness.

concepts.name: Electron dot structure of CO₂
concepts.simple_answer: Carbon dioxide CO₂: carbon forms double bonds with two oxygen atoms — O=C=O (linear molecule).
concepts.example: Product of complete combustion of carbon compounds.
concepts.remember: C forms 2 double bonds; linear shape.
concepts.common_confusion: CO₂ is inorganic — exception to organic rule.

concepts.name: Electron dot structure of H₂O
concepts.simple_answer: Water H₂O: oxygen shares one electron pair with each of two H atoms — two O–H single bonds; two lone pairs on O.
concepts.example: Product of complete combustion of hydrogen-containing fuels.
concepts.common_confusion: Bent shape due to lone pairs — beyond dot structure scope.

concepts.name: Exam — drawing Lewis structures
concepts.simple_answer: Count valence e⁻ → place least electronegative atom central → share pairs to complete octets → show lone pairs.
concepts.example: Draw CH₄, H₂O, CO₂ for practice.
concepts.remember: Share electrons until octet (duplet for H).
concepts.common_confusion: Do not forget lone pairs on O and N.

days.title: Allotropes of Carbon — Diamond, Graphite, Fullerene

concepts.name: What are allotropes?
concepts.simple_answer: Allotropes are different physical forms of the same element — same atoms, different arrangement and bonding.
concepts.example: Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon.

concepts.name: Diamond — structure and properties
concepts.simple_answer: Diamond: each carbon bonded to four others in a rigid 3D network — hardest natural substance, poor conductor, transparent.
concepts.example: Used in cutting tools and jewellery.
concepts.remember: 4 bonds per C; no free electrons.

concepts.name: Graphite — structure and properties
concepts.simple_answer: Graphite: carbon atoms in hexagonal layers held by weak forces — soft, slippery, good conductor (free electrons in layers).
concepts.example: Pencil lead and dry cell electrodes.
concepts.remember: 3 bonds per C; 1 free e⁻ per atom.

concepts.name: Diamond vs graphite comparison
concepts.simple_answer: Diamond: hard, insulator, 4 bonds per C. Graphite: soft, conductor, 3 bonds per C + free electron.

visual.formula: Diamond: hard, insulator | Graphite: soft, conductor

concepts.example: Same element — opposite electrical behaviour.
concepts.common_confusion: Both are pure carbon — different bonding arrangement.

concepts.name: Uses of diamond
concepts.simple_answer: Diamond used in jewellery (hardness, lustre) and industrial cutting/drilling due to extreme hardness.
concepts.example: Diamond-tipped glass cutters.

concepts.name: Uses of graphite
concepts.simple_answer: Graphite used in pencil leads, lubricants, electrodes (dry cells), and as moderator in nuclear reactors.
concepts.example: Pencil 'lead' is actually graphite.
concepts.common_confusion: Graphite is non-metal that conducts — Ch 3 link.

concepts.name: Fullerene C₆₀
concepts.simple_answer: Fullerene is an allotrope of carbon — cage-like molecule of 60 carbon atoms arranged like a football (soccer ball).
concepts.example: Discovered in 1985 — Nobel Prize 1996.

concepts.name: Why allotropes have different properties
concepts.simple_answer: Different arrangement of atoms and different bonding (sp³ in diamond vs sp² in graphite) cause different physical properties.
concepts.example: Diamond's 3D network vs graphite's layers.
concepts.remember: Bonding pattern determines hardness and conductivity.

concepts.name: Allotropes vs compounds
concepts.simple_answer: Allotropes are forms of one element; compounds contain two or more different elements chemically combined.

visual.formula: Allotrope: one element | Compound: two+ elements

concepts.example: Diamond (allotrope) vs CO₂ (compound).
concepts.common_confusion: O₂ and O₃ are allotropes of oxygen.

concepts.name: Exam — allotropes of carbon
concepts.simple_answer: Define allotrope → diamond (hard, insulator, 4 bonds) → graphite (soft, conductor, layers) → C₆₀ fullerene → compare uses.
concepts.example: Pencil lead = graphite; diamond ring = diamond.
concepts.common_confusion: Graphite conducts — important exception among non-metals.

concepts.name: What are hydrocarbons?
concepts.simple_answer: Hydrocarbons are compounds containing only carbon and hydrogen — the simplest organic compounds.
concepts.example: Methane CH₄ and ethene C₂H₄ are hydrocarbons.
concepts.common_confusion: All fossil fuels are mainly hydrocarbons.

concepts.name: Saturated hydrocarbons — alkanes
concepts.simple_answer: Saturated hydrocarbons have only single C–C and C–H bonds — all carbons bonded to maximum H; called alkanes.
concepts.example: Methane, ethane, propane are saturated.

concepts.name: General formula of alkanes
concepts.simple_answer: Alkanes follow CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ — for n carbons, hydrogens = 2n + 2.
concepts.example: Methane C₁H₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈.
concepts.common_confusion: C₁ = methane CH₄; C₂ = ethane C₂H₆.

concepts.name: Unsaturated hydrocarbons — introduction
concepts.simple_answer: Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain double or triple C–C bonds — not all carbons have maximum hydrogen.

visual.formula: Unsaturated = double or triple C–C bond

concepts.example: Ethene has C=C double bond.

concepts.name: Alkenes — general formula CₙH₂ₙ
concepts.simple_answer: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with one C=C double bond — general formula CₙH₂ₙ.
concepts.example: Ethene C₂H₄ (ethylene) and propene C₃H₆.

concepts.name: Alkynes — general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂
concepts.simple_answer: Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with one C≡C triple bond — general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
concepts.example: Ethyne C₂H₂ (acetylene) used in welding.

concepts.name: Examples — methane to ethyne
concepts.simple_answer: Methane CH₄ (alkane), ethene C₂H₄ (alkene), ethyne C₂H₂ (alkyne) — three families with two carbons.
concepts.example: Natural gas, fruit ripening, welding torch.

concepts.name: Single, double, and triple bonds
concepts.simple_answer: Single bond (C–C): one shared pair. Double (C=C): two shared pairs. Triple (C≡C): three shared pairs.

visual.formula: Single: 1 pair | Double: 2 pairs | Triple: 3 pairs

concepts.example: Ethane single; ethene double; ethyne triple.
concepts.remember: More shared pairs = shorter, stronger bond.

concepts.name: Compare saturated vs unsaturated
concepts.simple_answer: Saturated: single bonds, CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, less reactive. Unsaturated: double/triple bonds, more reactive, decolourise bromine water.

visual.formula: Saturated: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ | Unsaturated: CₙH₂ₙ or CₙH₂ₙ₋₂

concepts.example: Hexane saturated; hexene unsaturated.

concepts.name: Exam — hydrocarbon classification
concepts.simple_answer: Define hydrocarbon → saturated (alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂) → unsaturated (alkenes CₙH₂ₙ, alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂) → examples.
concepts.example: Give CH₄, C₂H₄, C₂H₂ as examples.
concepts.common_confusion: Do not confuse alkene and alkyne formulas.

days.title: Chains, Branches and Rings in Carbon Compounds

concepts.name: Straight chain carbon compounds
concepts.simple_answer: Straight chain compounds have carbon atoms linked in a continuous unbranched row — e.g. n-butane.
concepts.example: Pentane CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃ is straight chain.

concepts.name: Branched chain carbon compounds
concepts.simple_answer: Branched chains have a main chain with side groups (branches) attached — same formula, different structure.
concepts.example: Isobutane has a Y-shaped branch.
concepts.remember: Side chain branches off main chain.

concepts.name: Ring (cyclic) carbon compounds
concepts.simple_answer: Cyclic compounds have carbon atoms joined in a closed ring — e.g. cyclohexane C₆H₁₂.
concepts.example: Benzene ring (introductory mention in NCERT).
concepts.common_confusion: Ring compounds have different properties from chains.

concepts.name: Structural isomers — introduction
concepts.simple_answer: Compounds with same molecular formula but different structural arrangement are structural isomers.
concepts.example: Butane and isobutane both C₄H₁₀.
concepts.common_confusion: Isomerism adds to carbon's compound count.

concepts.name: Butane vs isobutane
concepts.simple_answer: n-Butane: straight chain C₄H₁₀. Isobutane: branched C₄H₁₀ — same formula, different boiling points.
concepts.example: Lighter fluid may contain isobutane.

concepts.name: Pentane isomers
concepts.simple_answer: Pentane C₅H₁₂ has three structural isomers: n-pentane, isopentane, and neopentane.
concepts.example: More carbons → more possible isomers.
concepts.common_confusion: Isomer count grows rapidly with carbon number.

concepts.name: Cyclohexane — ring example
concepts.simple_answer: Cyclohexane C₆H₁₂ is a saturated ring of six carbon atoms — each C bonded to two C and two H.
concepts.example: Six carbons in a ring — not straight chain.

concepts.name: Why carbon forms long chains
concepts.simple_answer: Catenation — carbon atoms link to each other strongly and repeatedly, forming chains of any length.
concepts.example: Paraffin wax has very long carbon chains.
concepts.remember: C bonds to C repeatedly = chains.
concepts.common_confusion: Carbon–carbon bonds are strong and stable.

concepts.name: Chains, branches, and rings together
concepts.simple_answer: Carbon compounds can combine straight chains, branches, and rings — adding enormous structural diversity.
concepts.example: Complex molecules like cholesterol have rings and branches.
concepts.common_confusion: Functional groups attach to any of these skeletons.

concepts.name: Exam — structural formulas
concepts.simple_answer: Draw straight chain → branched isomer → state same molecular formula → cyclohexane ring example.
concepts.example: Butane vs isobutane C₄H₁₀ comparison.
concepts.common_confusion: Same formula does not mean same compound.

concepts.name: Homologous series definition
concepts.simple_answer: A homologous series is a family of compounds with same functional group and similar chemical properties; successive members differ by CH₂.
concepts.example: Alkane series: CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈, C₄H₁₀.
concepts.remember: Same group; differ by CH₂ unit.
concepts.common_confusion: Members show gradual physical property change.

concepts.name: Successive members differ by CH₂
concepts.simple_answer: Each next member in a homologous series has one more CH₂ group — molecular mass increases by 14 u.
concepts.example: Ethane C₂H₆ to propane C₃H₈ adds CH₂.

concepts.name: Similar chemical properties in a series
concepts.simple_answer: All members of a homologous series react similarly because they have the same functional group.
concepts.example: All alkanes burn; all alcohols react with Na.

concepts.name: Gradual change in physical properties
concepts.simple_answer: Boiling point and melting point increase gradually down a homologous series as molecular size increases.
concepts.example: Methane gas; pentane liquid at room temp.
concepts.common_confusion: First four alkanes: gas → liquid trend.

concepts.name: Alcohol functional group — OH
concepts.simple_answer: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl functional group –OH attached to a carbon atom — e.g. ethanol C₂H₅OH.
concepts.example: Ethanol in drinks; methanol in industrial use.
concepts.common_confusion: Do not confuse with hydroxide ion OH⁻.

concepts.name: Aldehyde functional group — CHO
concepts.simple_answer: Aldehydes contain the –CHO (formyl) group — carbonyl at end of chain — e.g. methanal HCHO.
concepts.example: Formaldehyde HCHO preserves biological specimens.
concepts.common_confusion: Aldehyde vs ketone — position of C=O matters.

concepts.name: Ketone functional group — C=O
concepts.simple_answer: Ketones contain C=O (carbonyl) group between two carbon atoms — not at chain end — e.g. propanone.
concepts.example: Acetone (propanone) is a common solvent.
concepts.remember: C=O in middle of chain = ketone.
concepts.common_confusion: Aldehyde: C=O at end; ketone: C=O in middle.

concepts.name: Carboxylic acid functional group — COOH
concepts.simple_answer: Carboxylic acids contain –COOH (carboxyl) group — e.g. ethanoic acid CH₃COOH (acetic acid).
concepts.example: Vinegar contains ethanoic acid.
concepts.common_confusion: Acids turn blue litmus red — Ch 2 link.

concepts.name: Haloalkane functional group — X
concepts.simple_answer: Haloalkanes (alkyl halides) have a halogen (F, Cl, Br, I) attached to carbon — e.g. CH₃Cl chloromethane.
concepts.example: CH₃Cl formed in methane + Cl₂ substitution.

concepts.name: Exam — functional groups table
concepts.simple_answer: List –OH (alcohol), –CHO (aldehyde), C=O (ketone), –COOH (carboxylic acid), –X (halo) with one example each.
concepts.example: Ethanol, ethanoic acid, CH₃Cl as examples.

concepts.name: IUPAC naming basics
concepts.simple_answer: IUPAC system gives systematic names based on number of carbons (root) and functional group (suffix/prefix).
concepts.example: Ethanol = eth + an + ol (2C + alkane + alcohol).
concepts.common_confusion: Common names also used in NCERT.

concepts.name: Root word from carbon count
concepts.simple_answer: Root tells carbon count: meth- (1), eth- (2), prop- (3), but- (4), pent- (5), hex- (6).

visual.formula: meth=1, eth=2, prop=3, but=4, pent=5, hex=6

concepts.example: Eth- in ethanol means 2 carbons.

concepts.name: Suffix -ane for alkanes
concepts.simple_answer: Saturated hydrocarbons use suffix -ane: methane, ethane, propane, butane.
concepts.example: Propane C₃H₈ — prop + ane.

concepts.name: Suffix -ene for alkenes
concepts.simple_answer: Alkenes use suffix -ene for C=C double bond: ethene, propene, butene.
concepts.example: Ethene C₂H₄ — eth + ene.

concepts.name: Suffix -yne for alkynes
concepts.simple_answer: Alkynes use suffix -yne for C≡C triple bond: ethyne, propyne.
concepts.example: Ethyne C₂H₂ — eth + yne.

concepts.name: Naming with functional groups
concepts.simple_answer: Functional group suffix replaces -ane: -ol (alcohol), -oic acid (carboxylic), -al (aldehyde), -one (ketone).
concepts.example: Ethanol = eth + an + ol; ethanoic acid = eth + an + oic acid.
concepts.common_confusion: Longest chain including functional group carbon.

concepts.name: Examples — methanol, ethanol, ethanoic acid
concepts.simple_answer: Methanol CH₃OH (1C alcohol); ethanol C₂H₅OH (2C alcohol); ethanoic acid CH₃COOH (2C acid).
concepts.example: Methanol toxic; ethanol in beverages; vinegar = ethanoic acid.
concepts.common_confusion: Ethanoic acid also called acetic acid.

concepts.name: Common names vs IUPAC names
concepts.simple_answer: NCERT uses both: ethene/ethylene, ethyne/acetylene, ethanoic acid/acetic acid.

visual.formula: IUPAC and common names both valid

concepts.example: Write either name unless IUPAC specified.
concepts.remember: Learn pairs of common and IUPAC names.
concepts.common_confusion: Exam may use either — know both.

concepts.name: Position of functional group
concepts.simple_answer: When functional group can be at different positions, number the carbon chain to give lowest number to the group.
concepts.example: Propan-1-ol vs propan-2-ol — position matters.
concepts.remember: Number from end nearest functional group.

concepts.name: Exam — nomenclature practice
concepts.simple_answer: Identify root (C count) → identify functional group → add suffix → write full name with formula.
concepts.example: Name C₃H₇OH as propanol.

concepts.name: Combustion of carbon compounds
concepts.simple_answer: Combustion is reaction with oxygen releasing heat and light — carbon compounds burn to give CO₂ and H₂O on complete combustion.
concepts.example: Burning candle, petrol in engine.

concepts.name: Complete combustion
concepts.simple_answer: Complete combustion in sufficient O₂ gives CO₂ and H₂O — clean blue flame, no soot.
concepts.example: Bunsen burner with air hole open — blue flame.

concepts.name: Incomplete combustion
concepts.simple_answer: Incomplete combustion in limited O₂ gives carbon (soot), CO, and water — yellow smoky flame.
concepts.example: Yellow candle flame has soot at top.
concepts.common_confusion: CO is poisonous — see card below.

concepts.name: Combustion of methane
concepts.simple_answer: Methane burns completely: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat and light.
concepts.example: Natural gas stove burns methane.
concepts.remember: Balance C, H, O for full marks.

concepts.name: Combustion of ethanol
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanol burns with clean blue flame: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O + heat.
concepts.example: Spirit lamp burns ethanol.
concepts.remember: Ethanol burns cleanly — used as fuel.

concepts.name: Oxidation of alcohol to carboxylic acid
concepts.simple_answer: Alcohols oxidise to carboxylic acids using oxidising agents like alkaline KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇.
concepts.example: Ethanol oxidises to ethanoic acid.
concepts.common_confusion: Oxidising agents are coloured — purple KMnO₄ decolourises.

concepts.name: Oxidising agents — KMnO₄ and K₂Cr₂O₇
concepts.simple_answer: Potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) and potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) are common oxidising agents in NCERT.
concepts.example: Purple KMnO₄ decolourises when oxidising ethanol.
concepts.common_confusion: Also test for unsaturation in some contexts.

concepts.name: Dangers of carbon monoxide
concepts.simple_answer: CO from incomplete combustion is colourless, odourless, poisonous — binds to haemoglobin blocking O₂ transport.
concepts.example: Faulty gas heaters can produce CO.
concepts.common_confusion: Ensure good ventilation when burning fuels.

concepts.name: Soot from incomplete combustion
concepts.simple_answer: Soot is unburnt carbon particles from incomplete combustion — deposits on surfaces, causes air pollution.
concepts.example: Black deposit on bottom of cooking vessels.

concepts.name: Exam — combustion equations
concepts.simple_answer: Write complete combustion equation → balance → state products CO₂ + H₂O → contrast incomplete (soot, CO).
concepts.example: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O as model.

concepts.name: Addition reaction definition
concepts.simple_answer: Addition reaction: atoms add across a double or triple bond — unsaturated compound becomes saturated.
concepts.example: Ethene + H₂ → ethane is addition.
concepts.remember: Atoms add across C=C or C≡C.
concepts.common_confusion: Product has more H attached to carbons.

concepts.name: Unsaturated compounds undergo addition
concepts.simple_answer: Compounds with C=C or C≡C bonds open the multiple bond to add atoms — saturated compounds do not.
concepts.example: Ethene reacts; ethane does not (with H₂).

concepts.name: Ethene + H₂ → ethane (hydrogenation)
concepts.simple_answer: Ethene reacts with hydrogen in presence of Ni/Pt catalyst: C₂H₄ + H₂ → C₂H₆ (hydrogenation).
concepts.example: Used to convert vegetable oils to fats.
concepts.common_confusion: Ni or Pt catalyst needed for H₂ addition.

concepts.name: Ethene + Br₂ → dibromoethane
concepts.simple_answer: Ethene adds bromine: C₂H₄ + Br₂ → C₂H₄Br₂ (1,2-dibromoethane) — bromine adds across double bond.
concepts.example: Orange bromine decolourises when ethene added.
concepts.common_confusion: Product is saturated — no double bond left.

concepts.name: Bromine water test for unsaturation
concepts.simple_answer: Bromine water (orange) decolourises with unsaturated compounds — test for C=C double bond.
concepts.example: Ethene decolourises bromine water; ethane does not.
concepts.common_confusion: Bromine water is Br₂ dissolved in water.

concepts.name: Why bromine water decolourises
concepts.simple_answer: Bromine adds across the double bond in an addition reaction — orange Br₂ consumed, solution becomes colourless.
concepts.example: Shake ethene with bromine water — instant decolourisation.

concepts.name: Hydrogenation of vegetable oils
concepts.simple_answer: Unsaturated vegetable oils hydrogenated to saturated fats using H₂ and Ni catalyst — margarine production.
concepts.example: Margarine from hydrogenated oils.
concepts.remember: Addition of H₂ across C=C in oils.
concepts.common_confusion: Saturated fats have higher melting points.

concepts.name: Why saturated compounds do not undergo addition
concepts.simple_answer: Saturated compounds have only single bonds — no double/triple bond to open, so addition cannot occur.
concepts.example: Ethane does not decolourise bromine water.
concepts.remember: Single bonds already saturated with H.

concepts.name: Addition vs substitution
concepts.simple_answer: Addition: unsaturated + atoms across double bond. Substitution: saturated — one atom replaces another.
concepts.example: Ethene + Br₂ (addition); CH₄ + Cl₂ (substitution).
concepts.common_confusion: Do not mix up reaction types in exams.

concepts.name: Exam — addition reactions
concepts.simple_answer: Define addition → ethene + H₂ → ethane → ethene + Br₂ → bromine water test → hydrogenation of oils.
concepts.example: Write C₂H₄ + Br₂ → C₂H₄Br₂ with decolourisation.

concepts.name: Substitution reaction definition
concepts.simple_answer: Substitution: one atom or group replaces another in a saturated compound — no change in saturation.
concepts.example: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl.

concepts.name: Saturated compounds undergo substitution
concepts.simple_answer: Alkanes and other saturated compounds react by substitution — H replaced by halogen or other group.
concepts.example: Methane chlorination is classic example.

concepts.name: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (UV light)
concepts.simple_answer: Methane reacts with chlorine in sunlight/UV: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl — H replaced by Cl.
concepts.example: Chloromethane formed in photochemical reaction.
concepts.remember: Cl replaces one H; HCl by-product.

concepts.name: Role of sunlight or UV light
concepts.simple_answer: Chlorination of methane needs sunlight or UV — light energy breaks Cl–Cl bond to start free radical chain reaction.
concepts.example: No reaction in dark; rapid in sunlight.
concepts.common_confusion: Without light, methane and Cl₂ do not react at room temp.

concepts.name: Multiple substitution possible
concepts.simple_answer: Further substitution gives CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃, CCl₄ if excess Cl₂ and light — H replaced one by one.
concepts.example: Carbon tetrachloride CCl₄ is final chlorination product.
concepts.remember: Each step replaces one more H.
concepts.common_confusion: Products depend on Cl₂ amount and conditions.

concepts.name: Products of methane chlorination
concepts.simple_answer: Chloromethane CH₃Cl (methyl chloride), dichloromethane CH₂Cl₂, chloroform CHCl₃, carbon tetrachloride CCl₄.
concepts.example: Chloroform CHCl₃ was anaesthetic — now restricted.
concepts.remember: Know first product CH₃Cl for exam.

concepts.name: Why alkanes undergo substitution
concepts.simple_answer: Alkanes have strong C–H and C–C single bonds — they do not add across bonds; instead H is replaced.
concepts.example: Methane saturated — substitution only.
concepts.remember: No double bond to add across.

concepts.name: Chlorination vs bromination
concepts.simple_answer: Similar substitution with Br₂: CH₄ + Br₂ → CH₃Br + HBr — also needs light; bromination similar to chlorination.
concepts.example: Bromomethane CH₃Br formed similarly.

concepts.name: Substitution vs addition — summary
concepts.simple_answer: Substitution: saturated, one atom replaced (CH₄ + Cl₂). Addition: unsaturated, atoms add across double bond (C₂H₄ + Br₂).
concepts.example: Know which compound undergoes which.
concepts.common_confusion: Most common exam mistake — mixing types.

concepts.name: Exam — substitution reactions
concepts.simple_answer: Define substitution → CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (sunlight) → multiple products → contrast with addition.
concepts.example: Write balanced equation with light condition.

days.title: Important Carbon Compounds — Ethanol and Ethanoic Acid

concepts.name: Ethanol — structure C₂H₅OH
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanol (ethyl alcohol) has formula C₂H₅OH — two-carbon alcohol with –OH functional group.
concepts.example: Present in alcoholic beverages (dilute).

concepts.name: Uses of ethanol
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanol used as solvent, in medicines (tinctures), as fuel, and in beverages — versatile alcohol.
concepts.example: Iodine tincture is ethanol + iodine.

concepts.name: Denatured alcohol
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanol mixed with poisonous substances (methanol, pyridine) to make denatured alcohol — unfit for drinking, avoids tax.
concepts.example: Industrial ethanol sold as denatured spirit.
concepts.common_confusion: Denatured alcohol still flammable — handle carefully.

concepts.name: Ethanoic acid — structure CH₃COOH
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanoic acid (acetic acid) has formula CH₃COOH — two-carbon carboxylic acid, weak acid.
concepts.example: 5–8% solution in vinegar.

concepts.name: Acetic acid in vinegar
concepts.simple_answer: Vinegar is 5–8% ethanoic acid in water — sour taste and smell characteristic of carboxylic acids.
concepts.example: Salad dressing and pickling use vinegar.
concepts.common_confusion: Glacial acetic acid is nearly pure — corrosive.

concepts.name: Esterification — overview
concepts.simple_answer: Esterification: carboxylic acid reacts with alcohol in presence of conc. H₂SO₄ to form ester + water — sweet smell.
concepts.example: Ethanoic acid + ethanol → ethyl ethanoate.

concepts.name: Sweet smell of esters
concepts.simple_answer: Esters have pleasant fruity smell — used in perfumes and flavourings; formed in esterification.
concepts.example: Banana and apple flavours often esters.

concepts.name: Sources of ethanol
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanol produced by fermentation of sugars by yeast (anaerobic) and by hydration of ethene industrially.
concepts.example: Beer and wine production uses fermentation.

concepts.name: Sources of ethanoic acid
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanoic acid obtained by oxidation of ethanol or from bacterial fermentation of cider/vinegar.
concepts.example: Vinegar forms when wine exposed to air.
concepts.common_confusion: Bacteria Acetobacter oxidises ethanol in vinegar production.

concepts.name: Exam — ethanol and ethanoic acid
concepts.simple_answer: Give formulas C₂H₅OH and CH₃COOH → uses → denatured alcohol → esterification overview → vinegar.
concepts.example: Both compounds with structure and one use each.

days.title: Properties of Ethanol and Ethanoic Acid

concepts.name: Physical properties of ethanol
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanol is colourless liquid, miscible with water, volatile, burns with blue flame — good solvent.
concepts.example: Medical spirit is ethanol + water.

concepts.name: Ethanol reacts with sodium
concepts.simple_answer: Sodium reacts with ethanol to give sodium ethoxide and hydrogen: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂.
concepts.example: Sodium fizzes in ethanol — H₂ evolved.
concepts.remember: –OH H is slightly acidic — Na displaces H.

concepts.name: Dehydration of ethanol
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanol dehydrates to ethene on heating with conc. H₂SO₄ at 443 K: C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O.
concepts.example: Remove H₂O from ethanol → ethene.

concepts.name: Ethanol burns cleanly
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanol combustion: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O — clean blue flame, used as eco-friendly fuel.
concepts.example: Bioethanol mixed with petrol (gasohol).

concepts.name: Properties of ethanoic acid
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanoic acid is colourless liquid with pungent smell, sour taste, turns blue litmus red — weak acid.
concepts.example: Vinegar smell is ethanoic acid.

concepts.name: Ethanoic acid as weak acid
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanoic acid ionises partially in water: CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺ — weak acid, pH around 3 for vinegar.
concepts.example: Does not dissociate fully like HCl.
concepts.common_confusion: Turns blue litmus red — Ch 2 link.

concepts.name: Esterification equation — ethanoic acid + ethanol
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanoic acid + ethanol → ethyl ethanoate + water (conc. H₂SO₄ catalyst, heat).
concepts.example: Fruity smell confirms ester formed.

concepts.name: Role of conc. H₂SO₄ in esterification
concepts.simple_answer: Conc. H₂SO₄ acts as catalyst and dehydrating agent — speeds reaction and removes water to shift equilibrium.
concepts.example: Few drops of conc. H₂SO₄ added.
concepts.common_confusion: Do not confuse with dilute H₂SO₄ in other reactions.

concepts.name: Ethyl ethanoate — the ester product
concepts.simple_answer: Ethyl ethanoate CH₃COOC₂H₅ is the ester — pleasant smell used in nail polish remover and flavourings.
concepts.example: Sweet fruity smell in lab esterification.
concepts.remember: Name: ethyl (from ethanol) ethanoate (from ethanoic acid).

concepts.name: Exam — properties and reactions
concepts.simple_answer: Ethanol: Na reaction, dehydration, combustion. Ethanoic acid: weak acid, esterification equation with sweet smell.
concepts.example: Write esterification as key reaction.

days.title: Soaps and Detergents — Micelles and Cleansing Action

concepts.name: Soap structure — RCOO⁻Na⁺
concepts.simple_answer: Soap is sodium or potassium salt of long-chain carboxylic acid (fatty acid) — RCOO⁻Na⁺.
concepts.example: Sodium stearate is common soap component.

concepts.name: Saponification — making soap
concepts.simple_answer: Soap made by heating fat/oil with NaOH: fat + NaOH → soap + glycerol (saponification).
concepts.example: Traditional soap making from animal fat.
concepts.remember: Alkaline hydrolysis of ester in fat.

concepts.name: Micelle formation
concepts.simple_answer: In water, soap molecules form micelles — hydrophobic tails inward, hydrophilic heads outward facing water.
concepts.example: Spherical cluster of soap molecules in water.
concepts.remember: Tails hide inside; heads on surface.

concepts.name: Cleansing action of soap
concepts.simple_answer: Soap micelles surround oily dirt — hydrophobic tails dissolve grease inside micelle; rinsed away by water.
concepts.example: Oil on clothes removed by soap micelles.
concepts.remember: Emulsifies oil in water via micelles.

concepts.name: Hard water and soap scum
concepts.simple_answer: Hard water contains Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions — react with soap to form insoluble scum (curd), wasting soap.
concepts.example: White curd in bath with hard water + soap.
concepts.common_confusion: Scum is calcium/magnesium salt of fatty acid.

concepts.name: Why soap fails in hard water
concepts.simple_answer: Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ replace Na⁺ in soap forming insoluble precipitate — less soap available for cleaning.
concepts.example: Boiling hard water — scale on kettle.
concepts.common_confusion: Soft water (rainwater) lathers well with soap.

concepts.name: Detergent structure
concepts.simple_answer: Detergents are sodium salts of long-chain sulphonic acids or ammonium salts — similar tail, different head group.
concepts.example: Washing powder contains synthetic detergents.

concepts.name: Detergents work in hard water
concepts.simple_answer: Detergents do not form scum with Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ — soluble salts remain, effective in hard water.
concepts.example: Washing powder works in hard water areas.
concepts.remember: Ca/Mg salts of detergents stay soluble.
concepts.common_confusion: Main reason detergents replaced soap for laundry.

concepts.name: Soap vs detergent comparison
concepts.simple_answer: Soap: biodegradable, scum in hard water. Detergent: works in hard water, may persist in environment.

visual.formula: Soap: scum in hard water | Detergent: no scum

concepts.example: Soap better for environment; detergent better in hard water.
concepts.common_confusion: Some detergents are non-biodegradable — pollution concern.

concepts.name: Exam — micelle and cleansing action
concepts.simple_answer: Describe soap structure → micelle formation → hydrophobic tail dissolves grease → hard water scum → detergent advantage.
concepts.example: Draw micelle with tails inward.

days.title: Versatile Nature of Carbon — Catenation and Tetravalency

concepts.name: Catenation definition
concepts.simple_answer: Catenation is the ability of carbon atoms to link to each other in long chains, branches, and rings.
concepts.example: Carbon chains in petrol, proteins, DNA.
concepts.common_confusion: Carbon catenates more than any other element.

concepts.name: Tetravalency enables versatility
concepts.simple_answer: Carbon's four valence electrons allow four covalent bonds — single, double, triple, and bonds to many elements.
concepts.example: C can bond to C, H, O, N, S, halogens.

concepts.name: Millions of carbon compounds
concepts.simple_answer: Over 5 million carbon compounds known — more than all other elements combined — due to catenation and tetravalency.
concepts.example: Plastics, drugs, dyes, fuels — all carbon-based.

concepts.name: Self-linking of carbon atoms
concepts.simple_answer: Carbon–carbon bonds are strong and stable — carbon chains can be very long without breaking.
concepts.example: Polyethylene has thousands of linked carbons.
concepts.remember: Strong C–C bonds hold chains together.
concepts.common_confusion: Silicon catenates but Si–Si weaker than C–C.

concepts.name: Single, double, triple bond variety
concepts.simple_answer: Carbon forms single (C–C), double (C=C), and triple (C≡C) bonds — multiplying possible structures.
concepts.example: Alkanes, alkenes, alkynes from bond types.
concepts.remember: Three bond types × long chains = huge variety.

concepts.name: Functional groups add diversity
concepts.simple_answer: Same carbon skeleton with different functional groups (–OH, –COOH, –CHO) gives entirely different compounds.
concepts.example: Ethanol and dimethyl ether both C₂H₆O — different groups.
concepts.remember: Same formula possible with different groups.

concepts.name: Isomerism adds more compounds
concepts.simple_answer: Same molecular formula, different structures (isomers) — butane/isobutane, functional group isomers.
concepts.example: C₄H₁₀ has two structural isomers.
concepts.common_confusion: Millions of compounds include all isomers.

concepts.name: Role of carbon in living organisms
concepts.simple_answer: All biomolecules — carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids — are carbon compounds with complex chains and rings.
concepts.example: DNA double helix is carbon backbone.

concepts.name: Scope of organic chemistry
concepts.simple_answer: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds — synthesis, reactions, and applications in medicine, industry, and life.
concepts.example: Pharmaceuticals, polymers, food additives.
concepts.common_confusion: Class 10 Ch 4 is introduction to organic chemistry.

concepts.name: Exam — why carbon is unique
concepts.simple_answer: State tetravalency + catenation → chains/branches/rings → functional groups → isomerism → millions of compounds + life.
concepts.example: Link both properties to compound count.
concepts.remember: Two properties + three diversity sources + example.
concepts.common_confusion: Do not forget catenation AND tetravalency together.

days.title: Mixed Review — Hydrocarbons and Functional Groups

concepts.name: Review — saturated vs unsaturated
concepts.simple_answer: Saturated: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, single bonds, substitution. Unsaturated: CₙH₂ₙ or CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, addition, bromine test.
concepts.example: Methane vs ethene comparison.

concepts.name: Review — functional groups
concepts.simple_answer: –OH alcohol, –CHO aldehyde, C=O ketone, –COOH carboxylic acid, –X haloalkane — determine chemical properties.
concepts.example: Ethanol, ethanoic acid, CH₃Cl examples.

concepts.name: Review — allotropes of carbon
concepts.simple_answer: Diamond: hard, insulator, 4 bonds. Graphite: soft, conductor, layers. Fullerene C₆₀: cage structure.
concepts.example: Pencil lead = graphite; diamond ring.

concepts.name: Review — homologous series
concepts.simple_answer: Same functional group, differ by CH₂, similar chemical properties, gradual physical property change.
concepts.example: Alkane series CH₄ to C₄H₁₀.

concepts.name: Review — combustion
concepts.simple_answer: Complete: CO₂ + H₂O (blue flame). Incomplete: soot + CO (yellow flame). CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.

visual.formula: Complete: CO₂ + H₂O | Incomplete: C + CO

concepts.example: Balanced methane combustion equation.

concepts.name: Review — addition vs substitution
concepts.simple_answer: Addition: unsaturated (C₂H₄ + Br₂). Substitution: saturated (CH₄ + Cl₂, UV). Know conditions.

visual.formula: Addition: C₂H₄ + Br₂ | Substitution: CH₄ + Cl₂

concepts.example: Bromine water test for addition.

concepts.name: Review — ethanol and ethanoic acid
concepts.simple_answer: C₂H₅OH (solvent, fuel) and CH₃COOH (vinegar, weak acid) — esterification links them.
concepts.example: Esterification sweet smell test.

concepts.name: Review — soaps and detergents
concepts.simple_answer: Soap RCOO⁻Na⁺, micelle cleans, scum in hard water. Detergent works in hard water — no scum.
concepts.example: Micelle: tails in, heads out.

concepts.name: Review — Lewis structures
concepts.simple_answer: CH₄ (4 single), C₂H₆ (C–C + 6 C–H), O₂ (double), N₂ (triple), CO₂ (2 double), H₂O (2 single + lone pairs).

visual.formula: CH₄ | C₂H₆ | O₂ | N₂ | CO₂ | H₂O

concepts.example: Draw all six for exam practice.
concepts.remember: Six key Lewis structures from NCERT.
concepts.common_confusion: Show lone pairs on O and N.

concepts.name: Review — nomenclature
concepts.simple_answer: Roots meth– to hex–; suffixes -ane, -ene, -yne, -ol, -oic acid; examples ethanol, ethanoic acid.
concepts.example: Propene C₃H₆; propanol C₃H₇OH.

days.title: Exam Prep — Reactions, Nomenclature and Everyday Chemistry

concepts.name: Exam — Lewis structures template
concepts.simple_answer: Count valence e⁻ → central atom → share to complete octets → CH₄, H₂O, CO₂, O₂, N₂, C₂H₆.
concepts.example: Practice drawing all six structures.
concepts.common_confusion: Duplet for H; octet for C, O, N.

concepts.name: Exam — hydrocarbon formulas
concepts.simple_answer: Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkenes CₙH₂ₙ, alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ — give examples CH₄, C₂H₄, C₂H₂.
concepts.example: Three formulas with two-carbon examples.

concepts.name: Exam — reaction types summary
concepts.simple_answer: Combustion (CO₂ + H₂O), addition (unsaturated + Br₂), substitution (CH₄ + Cl₂, UV), esterification (acid + alcohol).
concepts.example: One equation per reaction type.

concepts.name: Exam — functional groups table
concepts.simple_answer: Tabulate –OH, –CHO, C=O, –COOH, –X with name, example, and one property each.
concepts.example: Ethanol, ethanoic acid, CH₃Cl as examples.

concepts.name: Exam — bromine water test
concepts.simple_answer: Unsaturated compound + bromine water → decolourisation (addition). Saturated → no change.
concepts.example: Ethene positive; ethane negative.

concepts.name: Exam — esterification
concepts.simple_answer: Acid + alcohol → ester + water; conc. H₂SO₄ catalyst; sweet smell confirms product.
concepts.example: Ethyl ethanoate — fruity smell.

concepts.name: Exam — soap micelle description
concepts.simple_answer: Soap RCOO⁻Na⁺ → micelle in water → hydrophobic tail dissolves grease → hard water scum → detergent alternative.
concepts.example: Describe micelle structure in words.
concepts.common_confusion: Include saponification if asked for preparation.

concepts.name: Exam — incomplete combustion
concepts.simple_answer: Limited O₂ → soot (C) + CO + H₂O; CO poisonous; complete combustion gives CO₂ + H₂O only.
concepts.example: Yellow flame = incomplete.

concepts.name: Unit 4 exam — full revision summary
concepts.simple_answer: Bonding → allotropes → hydrocarbons → functional groups → reactions → ethanol/acid → soaps → catenation/tetravalency.
concepts.example: 160 concept cards cover all topics.
concepts.remember: Three pillars: structure, reactions, daily life.
concepts.common_confusion: Link structure to reactivity in answers.
